title: yadgar/iam-db
$comment: CLOSED PER CHART (ADR-0847, ADR-0850, ledger 990): this schema closes every key iam-db's own values.yaml declares and refuses an unknown one at render. It closes only what this chart owns -- a parent or platform that embeds iam-db leaves this whole section open instead of re-declaring it. OPEN MAPS, left as `{}` on purpose: `global` (injected by a parent/platform at render time; this chart reads none of it itself, but a closed root would refuse the key the moment it is embedded); `resources` and `database.instance.resources` (plain Kubernetes ResourceRequirements, handed straight to `toYaml`, whose own shape is not this chart's to validate); `rollingUpdate` (same, handed to `toYaml` under `strategy.rollingUpdate`). EXTRAS, declared as leaves though `values.yaml` never states them: `image.digest` (absent from `values.yaml` by design -- `ci-release` rewrites it at package time, D65); `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom.namespace` (`values.yaml` ships `scrapeFrom: {}`; `templates/networkpolicy.yaml` reads the key under it). TYPES, TOGGLES AND `required` ON A NEW KEY ARE NOT THIS FILE'S JOB (ADR-0847): `chart/templates/render-checks.yaml` validates `database.create` and `autoscaling.enabled` with `kindIs "bool"` and raises its own named refusal; nothing here duplicates that. The two exceptions predate this closure and are kept unchanged: `database` carries `type: object` and `required: [migrationLockTimeoutSeconds]` (ledger 814, ADR-0837) -- `database.migrationLockTimeoutSeconds` is the one knob this file bounds as `integer, 1..590`, because the binary reads it with no fallback. There is no root `required`: `database` deleted outright is still refused by the chart's own render check (`database` is absent from the values), with a more specific sentence than a schema line would give, and `tls.enabled` is not required here -- that lands in C-DB1 (ADR-0845, K-8), never in D-S.

migrationLockTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds a replica waits for another one's migration before failing its boot. Rendered as DB_MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and read with no fallback. Minimum 1: GET_LOCK with 0 never waits and with a negative wait never takes the lock. Maximum 590: see chart/values.yaml.
